claim: The Golgi apparatus was discovered 120 years ago.
source: Although this organelle was discovered 120 years ago, such basic questions as whether vesicular transport through the Golgi occurs in an anterograde (from entry to exit) or retrograde fashion are still strongly debated.
evidence: This is a historical fact stated in the introduction to contextualize the long-standing nature of questions about Golgi function.

claim: Whether vesicular transport through the Golgi occurs in an anterograde or retrograde fashion is still strongly debated.
source: Although this organelle was discovered 120 years ago, such basic questions as whether vesicular transport through the Golgi occurs in an anterograde (from entry to exit) or retrograde fashion are still strongly debated.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of scientific debate in the field.

claim: Anterograde or retrograde vesicular transports are asymptotic behaviors of a much richer dynamical system.
source: We show that anterograde or retrograde vesicular transports are asymptotic behaviors of a much richer dynamical system.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: The structure and composition of cellular compartments and the directionality of vesicular exchange are intimately linked.
source: Indeed, the structure and composition of cellular compartments and the directionality of vesicular exchange are intimately linked.
evidence: This is a key conclusion derived from the model's results.

claim: The structure and composition of cellular compartments and the directionality of vesicular exchange are emergent properties that can be tuned by varying the relative rates of vesicle budding, fusion and biochemical conversion.
source: They are emergent properties that can be tuned by varying the relative rates of vesicle budding, fusion and biochemical conversion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the model simulations.

claim: The Golgi apparatus is an intracellular organelle at the crossroad of the secretory, lysosomal and endocytic pathways.
source: The Golgi apparatus is an intracellular organelle at the crossroad of the secretory, lysosomal and endocytic pathways (Heald and Cohen-Fix, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: One of the Golgi's most documented functions is the sorting and processing of many proteins synthesized by eukaryotic cells.
source: One of its most documented functions is the sorting and processing of many proteins synthesized by eukaryotic cells (Lippincott-Schwartz et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Proteins translated in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are addressed to the Golgi, where they undergo post-translational maturation and sorting, before being exported to their final destination.
source: Proteins translated in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are addressed to the Golgi, where they undergo post-translational maturation and sorting, before being exported to their final destination.
evidence: This describes the established pathway of protein processing.

claim: The Golgi itself is composed of distinct sub-compartments, called cisternae, of different biochemical identities.
source: The Golgi itself is composed of distinct sub-compartments, called cisternae, of different biochemical identities (Stanley, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: From the ER, cargo-proteins successively reside in cisternae of the cis, medial and trans-identities, after which they exit the Golgi via the trans-Golgi network (TGN).
source: From the ER, cargo-proteins successively reside in cisternae of the cis, medial and trans-identities, after which they exit the Golgi via the trans-Golgi network (TGN).
evidence: This describes the established progression of cargo through the Golgi.

claim: In yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, cisternae are dispersed throughout the cell.
source: In some organisms such as the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae cisternae are dispersed throughout the cell (Suda and Nakano, 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: In yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, each cisterna undergoes maturation from a cis to a trans-identity.
source: In some organisms such as the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae cisternae are dispersed throughout the cell (Suda and Nakano, 2012) and each cisterna undergoes maturation from a cis to a trans-identity (Losev et al., 2006; Matsuura-Tokita et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental observations.

claim: In most eukaryotes other than yeast, cisternae are stacked in a polarized fashion, with cargo-proteins entering via the cis-face and exiting via the trans-face.
source: In most other eukaryotes, cisternae are stacked in a polarized fashion, with cargo-proteins entering via the cis-face and exiting via the trans-face (Boncompain and Perez, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Golgi polarity is robustly conserved over time, despite cisternae constantly exchanging vesicles with each other, the ER and the TGN.
source: This polarity is robustly conserved over time, despite cisternae constantly exchanging vesicles with each other, the ER and the TGN (Lippincott-Schwartz et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Pharmacological treatments that alter the structure and stacking of Golgi compartments in mammalian cells affect the processing of certain proteins, particularly glycosylation.
source: Pharmacological treatments that alter the structure and stacking of Golgi compartments in mammalian cells affect the processing of certain proteins, and in particular glycosylation (Hu et al., 2005; Shen et al., 2007; Xiang et al., 2013; Bekier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: The highly dynamical nature and compact structure of a stacked Golgi makes it difficult to determine how cargo-proteins are transported in an anterograde fashion from the cis to trans-side of the stack.
source: The highly dynamical nature and compact structure of a stacked Golgi makes it difficult to determine how cargo-proteins are transported in an anterograde fashion from the cis to trans-side of the stack and how this transport is coupled to processing.
evidence: This describes a challenge in the field based on the physical properties of the Golgi.

claim: Several models have been proposed to explain the transport dynamics of Golgi cargo, mostly belonging to two classes: one involving stable compartments exchanging components through fusion-based mechanisms and one involving transient compartments undergoing en-block maturation.
source: Several models have been proposed to explain the transport dynamics of Golgi cargo (See sketch in Figure 1A). They mostly belong to two classes: one involving stable compartments exchanging components through fusion-based mechanisms and one involving transient compartments undergoing en-block maturation and in which fusion mechanisms are dispensable for cargo transport.
evidence: This summarizes existing models in the literature, with reference to a figure.

claim: The 'Vesicular transport' model postulated that cisternae have fixed identities and cargo progresses from one cisterna to the next via anterograde vesicular transport.
source: Historically (Malhotra and Mayor, 2006), the 'Vesicular transport' model postulated that cisternae have fixed identities and cargo progresses from one cisterna to the next via anterograde vesicular transport
evidence: This describes a historical model with citation support.

claim: The 'Cisternal Maturation' model postulated that cisternae themselves undergo maturation from the cis to the trans-identity and physically move through the stack, while Golgi resident proteins remain in the stack by moving toward the cis-face by retrograde vesicular transport.
source: while the 'Cisternal Maturation' model postulated that cisternae themselves undergo maturation from the cis to the trans-identity and physically move through the stack, while Golgi resident proteins remain in the stack by moving toward the cis-face by retrograde vesicular transport.
evidence: This describes a historical model.

claim: Extensions of the vesicular transport and cisternal maturation models have been proposed, including cisternal maturation with tubular connections.
source: Several extensions of these two models have been proposed, including cisternal maturation with tubular connections (Trucco et al., 2004; Rizzo et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: The rapid partitioning model proposes rapid partitioning within Golgi cisternae between processing and exporting sub-compartments.
source: rapid partitioning within Golgi cisternae between processing and exporting sub-compartments (Patterson et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: The cisternal progenitor model proposes that stable cisternae exchange material by the fusion and fission of sub-compartments defined by their composition of Rab GTPases, which evolve over time through exchange with the cytosol.
source: or the cisternal progenitor model (Pfeffer, 2010), in which stable cisternae exchange material by the fusion and fission of sub-compartments defined by their composition of Rab GTPases, which evolve over time through exchange with the cytosol.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: Existing Golgi transport models do not provide a quantitative analysis of the generation and maintenance of Golgi compartments.
source: It is noteworthy that these models do not provide a quantitative analysis of the generation and maintenance of Golgi compartments, nor do they attempt to relate the Golgi structure (number and size of compartments) and transport dynamics.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of the literature.

claim: Much remains unknown regarding the mechanisms that dictate the organisation and dynamics of the Golgi.
source: Therefore, much remains unknown regarding the mechanisms that dictate the organisation and dynamics of the Golgi.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: There is a large diversity in Golgi structures and dynamics among different species.
source: Although there is a large diversity in Golgi structures and dynamics among different species, the physiological function of the organelle as a sorting and processing hub is common to all species
evidence: This is based on comparative biology knowledge.

claim: The physiological function of the Golgi as a sorting and processing hub is common to all species.
source: Although there is a large diversity in Golgi structures and dynamics among different species, the physiological function of the organelle as a sorting and processing hub is common to all species
evidence: This is based on comparative biology knowledge.

claim: Important mechanisms controlling Golgi dynamics are conserved across species.
source: suggesting that important mechanisms controlling Golgi dynamics are conserved.
evidence: This is inferred from the conservation of function despite structural diversity.

claim: Different classes of mathematical models of Golgi dynamics have been proposed, including models based on rate equations.
source: Different classes of mathematical models have been proposed, from models of vesicle budding and fusion based on rate equations (Binder et al., 2009; Ispolatov and Müsch, 2013; Mukherji and O'Shea, 2014) - some specifically including space (Sachdeva et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: Continuous, discrete and stochastic models of protein sorting in the Golgi have been proposed.
source: to continuous, discrete and stochastic models of protein sorting in the Golgi (Gong et al., 2010; Vagne and Sens, 2018b)
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: Computer simulations based on membrane mechanics have been used to model the Golgi.
source: and computer simulations based on membrane mechanics (Tachikawa and Mochizuki, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: The Golgi can reassemble after mitosis.
source: To account for the ability of the Golgi to reassemble after mitosis (Wei and Seemann, 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: Many studies have sought to describe the Golgi as a self-organized system.
source: many of these studies have sought to describe the Golgi as a self-organized system (Binder et al., 2009; Kühnle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: The manner in which the kinetics of the Golgi's two main functions (transport and biochemical conversion) interplay to yield a robust steady-state has received much less attention.
source: However, the manner in which the kinetics of the Golgi two main functions (namely the transport and biochemical conversion of its components) interplay with one another to yield a robust steady-state has so far received much less attention (Sachdeva et al., 2016; Vagne and Sens, 2018b).
evidence: This is an assessment of the literature with citations.

claim: Most existing models discuss transport through a pre-existing compartmentalised Golgi structure.
source: Most existing models discuss transport through a pre-existing compartmentalised Golgi structure.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of existing models.

claim: The main goal of the model is to explain how compartmentalised structure and flux can spontaneously emerge through self-organisation.
source: The main goal of our model is to explain how this compartmentalised structure and the flux within it can spontaneously emerge through self-organisation.
evidence: This states the primary objective of the study.

claim: In the model, both Golgi self-organisation and vesicular transport are solely directed by local molecular interactions resulting in composition-dependent budding and fusion.
source: We propose here a model in which both Golgi self-organisation and vesicular transport are solely directed by (local) molecular interactions resulting in composition-dependent budding and fusion.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the model design.

claim: The model neglects the spatial structure of the Golgi and assumes that any two components of the system can interact with one another.
source: In particular, we neglect the spatial structure of the Golgi, and assume that any two components of the system can interact with one another (see the Discussion section for the relevance of this approximation).
evidence: This describes a key assumption of the model.

claim: The directionality of vesicular transport is an emergent property of the self-organisation process that co-evolves with the size and number of Golgi sub-compartments.
source: Thus, the directionality of vesicular transport is an emergent property of the self-organisation process that co-evolves with the size and number of Golgi sub-compartments, rather than being fixed by arbitrary rules.
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: The model highlights the link between the large-scale steady-state organisation of the Golgi, the directionality of vesicular transport, and the kinetics of individual processes at the molecular scale.
source: This approach brings new conceptual insights that highlight the link between the large-scale steady-state organisation of the Golgi, the directionality of vesicular transport, and the kinetics of individual processes at the molecular scale.
evidence: This describes a key insight from the model.

claim: A wide variety of organelle phenotypes can be observed upon varying the rates of the local processes.
source: We show that a wide variety of organelle phenotypes can be observed upon varying the rates of the local processes.
evidence: This is a finding from the model simulations.

claim: The model uncovers a correlation between the size and composition (purity) of Golgi sub-compartments.
source: In particular, our model uncovers a correlation between the size and composition (purity) of Golgi sub-compartments.
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: Composition-dependent exchange between compartments yields complex vesicular flux patterns that are neither purely anterograde nor purely retrograde.
source: Besides, it emphasizes that composition-dependent exchange between compartments yields complex vesicular flux patterns that are neither purely anterograde (as in the 'vesicular transport' model) nor purely retrograde (as in the 'cisternal maturation' model).
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: The system is discretised at the scale of small vesicles, which define the unit size of the system.
source: The system is discretised at the scale of small vesicles, which define the unit size of the system.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the model design.

claim: Vesicles can fuse together or with existing compartments to form larger compartments and can bud from compartments.
source: Vesicles can fuse together or with existing compartments to form larger compartments and can bud from compartments.
evidence: This describes the dynamics included in the model.

claim: Compartments consist of a number of membrane patches with distinct identities.
source: Compartments consist of a number of membrane patches (of size unity) with distinct identities.
evidence: This describes the structure of compartments in the model.

claim: The biochemical identity of a membrane patch is defined by its composition in lipids and proteins that influence its interaction with other patches, such as Rab GTPases or fusion proteins such as SNAREs.
source: The biochemical identity of a membrane patch is defined in a very broad sense by its composition in lipids and proteins that influence its interaction with other patches, such as Rab GTPases (Grosshans et al., 2006) or fusion proteins such as SNAREs (Cai et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes the biological basis for the model's identity concept, with citations.

claim: Vesicles and membrane patches are of either cis, medial or trans-identity, consistent with the three main biochemical identities reported for Golgi membranes.
source: Consistently with the three main biochemical identities reported for Golgi membranes (Day et al., 2013), vesicles and membrane patches are of either cis, medial or trans-identity
evidence: This describes a model feature based on biological knowledge with citation.

claim: Membrane patches can undergo irreversible biochemical conversion from the cis to the trans-identity.
source: and can undergo irreversible biochemical conversion from the cis to the trans-identity.
evidence: This describes a key process in the model.

claim: Vesicles and compartments can fuse homotypically with the ER (itself of cis identity) and the TGN (of trans identity).
source: and vesicles and compartments can fuse homotypically with the ER (itself of cis identity) and the TGN (of trans identity).
evidence: This describes exit mechanisms in the model.

claim: The stationary size distribution of compartments is a decreasing function of the compartment size, which typically shows a power law decay at small size, with an exponential cut-off at large size.
source: The stationary size distribution of compartments is a decreasing function of the compartment size, which typically shows a power law decay at small size, with an exponential cut-off at large size (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations shown in a figure.

claim: The size distribution pattern (power law with exponential cut-off) is expected for a non-equilibrium steady-state controlled by scission and aggregation.
source: This is expected for a non-equilibrium steady-state controlled by scission and aggregation (Turner et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to theoretical work.

claim: There exist many small compartments and very few large ones in the steady-state.
source: and means that there exist many small compartments and very few large ones.
evidence: This is inferred from the size distribution.

claim: Mixing occurs by biochemical conversion and sorting occurs by budding of contaminating species.
source: This can be understood by analyzing the processes involved in mixing and sorting of different identities. In a first approximation, mixing occurs by biochemical conversion and sorting occurs by budding of contaminating species
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model mechanisms.

claim: The archetypal behaviors (anterograde and retrograde transport) most often discussed in the literature are asymptotic regimes for extreme values of the ratio of budding to fusion rates.
source: The archetypal behaviors most often discussed in the literature are thus, within the limits of our model, asymptotic regimes for extreme values of the ratio of budding to fusion rates.
evidence: This is a key interpretation of the model results in relation to existing literature.

claim: In the model, vesicle budding and fusion are biased solely by local compositions, which is subjected to irreversible biochemical conversions.
source: In our model organelle, vesicle budding and fusion are biased solely by local compositions, which is subjected to irreversible biochemical conversions.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the model design.

claim: The interplay between microscopic processes (budding, fusion, biochemical conversion) gives rise to an irreversible flux of vesicles across the system.
source: The interplay between these microscopic processes gives rise to an irreversible flux of vesicles across the system.
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: At low budding rate, the system is dominated by compartment maturation, and the compartment distribution is spread around a path going from purely cis to purely trans-compartments.
source: The system is dominated by compartment maturation, and the compartment distribution is spread around a path going from purely cis to purely trans-compartments, consistent with a dynamics where each compartment maturates independently from the other and given by Equation 9.
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations and analytical approximation.

claim: At low budding rate, the majority of the transport vesicles are emitted by trans-rich compartments, which concentrate most of the components of the system, leading to a retrograde vesicular flux.
source: The majority of the transport vesicles are emitted by trans-rich compartments, which concentrate most of the components of the system, leading to a retrograde vesicular flux.
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: At high budding rate, compartments are exclusively distributed along the cis/medial and medial/trans-axes of composition, and accumulate at the vertices of the triangle.
source: Compartments are exclusively distributed along the cis/medial and medial/trans-axes of composition, and accumulate at the vertices of the triangle.
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: At high budding rate, membrane patches that just underwent conversion bud quickly from the donor compartment and fuse with pure compartments with the appropriate medial or trans-identity, explaining the clear anterograde vesicular transport.
source: Membrane patches that just underwent conversion bud quickly from the donor compartment and fuse with pure compartments with the appropriate medial or trans-identity, explaining the clear anterograde vesicular transport.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model mechanisms.

claim: In the intermediate regime, the distribution of mixed compartments is more homogeneous along the line describing the maturation of individual compartments.
source: In the intermediate regime (middle row in Figure 4), the distribution of mixed compartments is more homogeneous along the line describing the maturation of individual compartments - both in terms of size and number of compartments.
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the intermediate regime, cis-rich and trans-rich compartments emit comparable amount of transport vesicles, while large medial-rich compartments are absent, leading to a centripetal vesicular flux with an enrichment in medial identity.
source: Cis-rich and trans-rich compartments emit comparable amount of transport vesicles, while large medial-rich compartments are absent. This leads to a centripetal vesicular flux with an enrichment in medial identity (see Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: The lack of large medial-rich compartment is due to the fact that they can be contaminated by either cis or trans-species and fuse with cis-rich or trans-rich compartments.
source: The lack of large medial-rich compartment is due to the fact that they can be contaminated by either cis or trans-species and fuse with cis-rich or trans-rich compartments.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model mechanisms.

claim: The model does not include space, so it does not refer to the spatial structure of a stacked Golgi, but rather to the self-organisation of Golgi components into compartments of distinct identities undergoing vesicular exchange.
source: As our model does not include space, we do not refer to the spatial structure of a stacked Golgi, but rather to the self-organisation of Golgi components into compartments of distinct identities undergoing vesicular exchange.
evidence: This clarifies the scope of the model.

claim: Directional vesicular exchanges between compartments of different identities spontaneously emerge from local biochemical interactions, despite the absence of spatial information.
source: We show that directional vesicular exchanges between compartments of different identities spontaneously emerge from local biochemical interactions, despite the absence of spatial information.
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: The Golgi functionality is preserved under major perturbation of its spatial structure resulting from land-locking Golgi cisternae to mitochondria.
source: This is in line with recent observations that the Golgi functionality is preserved under major perturbation of its spatial structure resulting from land-locking Golgi cisternae to mitochondria (Dunlop et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: Cargo transport still proceeds in land-locked Golgi, and is merely slowed down by a factor of two (from 20 min to 40 min) despite the absence of spatial proximity between cisternae.
source: Indeed, cargo transport still proceed, and is merely slowed down by a factor of two (from 20 min to 40 min) in land-locked Golgi despite the absence of spatial proximity between cisternae.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations from the cited study.

claim: Spatial information is less crucial to the Golgi function than biochemical information.
source: This suggests that spatial information is less crucial to the Golgi function than biochemical information.
evidence: This is inferred from the land-locking experiments.

claim: The steady-state organisation of the organelle, in terms of size and composition of its compartments, is intimately linked to the directionality of vesicular exchange between compartments through the mechanism of homotypic fusion.
source: Our main result is that the steady-state organisation of the organelle, in terms of size and composition of its compartments, is intimately linked to the directionality of vesicular exchange between compartments through the mechanism of homotypic fusion.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the model.

claim: Both the steady-state organisation and directionality of vesicular exchange are controlled by a kinetic competition between vesicular exchange and biochemical conversion.
source: Both aspects are controlled by a kinetic competition between vesicular exchange and biochemical conversion.
evidence: This is a key conclusion from the model.

claim: The predicted role of the budding and fusion rates is in agreement with the phenotype observed upon deletion of Arf1, which decreases the number of compartments and increases their size, particularly that of trans-compartments.
source: The predicted role of the budding and fusion rates is in agreement with the phenotype observed upon deletion of Arf1 (a protein involved in vesicle budding), which decreases the number of compartments and increases their size, particularly that of trans-compartments which seem to aggregate into one major cisterna (Bhave et al., 2014).
evidence: This compares model predictions with experimental observations.

claim: A comparable phenotype to Arf1 deletion has been observed upon mutation of NSF (a fusion protein), which produces extremely large, but transient, trans-compartments.
source: A comparable phenotype has been observed upon mutation of NSF (a fusion protein), which produces extremely large, but transient, trans-compartments (Tanabashi et al., 2018), thereby increasing the stochasticity of the system.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: Modifying the expression of VPS74 leads to an altered Golgi organisation, comparable to the ARF1 deletion phenotype.
source: Modifying the expression of VPS74 (yeast homolog of GOLPH3) leads to an altered Golgi organisation, comparable to the ARF1 deletion phenotype (Iyer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: The correlation between the size and purity of the compartments predicted by the model is in agreement with the observation that decreasing the budding rate by altering the activity of COPI leads to larger and less sorted compartments.
source: Importantly, the correlation between the size and purity of the compartments predicted by our model is in agreement with the observation that decreasing the budding rate by altering the activity of COPI (a budding protein) leads to larger and less sorted compartments (Papanikou et al., 2015).
evidence: This compares model predictions with experimental observations.

claim: Over-expression of Ypt1 (a Rab protein) increases the transition rate from early to transitional Golgi, and increases the co-localization of early and late Golgi markers.
source: In yeast again, over-expression of Ypt1 (a Rab protein) increases the transition rate from early to transitional Golgi, and increases the co-localization of early and late Golgi markers (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: One crucial model prediction is that the size and purity of Golgi compartments should be affected in a correlated fashion by physiological perturbations.
source: One crucial model prediction is that the size and purity of Golgi compartments should be affected in a correlated fashion by physiological perturbations.
evidence: This is a testable prediction from the model.

claim: The directionality of vesicular transport is intimately linked to the steady-state organisation of the organelle; vesicular transport is anterograde when compartments are pure, and it is retrograde when they are mixed.
source: The directionality of vesicular transport is intimately linked to the steady-state organisation of the organelle; vesicular transport is anterograde when compartments are pure, and it is retrograde when they are mixed.
evidence: This is a key finding from the model.

claim: If budding is faster than biochemical conversion, the contaminating species is the one that just underwent conversion, and its budding and fusion with more mature compartment leads to an anterograde transport.
source: If budding is faster than biochemical conversion, the contaminating species is the one that just underwent conversion, and its budding and fusion with more mature compartment leads to an anterograde transport.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model mechanisms.

claim: If biochemical conversion is faster than budding, the contaminating species is the less mature one, leading to a retrograde transport.
source: If biochemical conversion is faster than budding, the contaminating species is the less mature one, leading to a retrograde transport.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model mechanisms.

claim: The directionality of vesicular exchange is an emergent property intimately linked to the purity of the compartments.
source: Thus, the directionality of vesicular exchange is an emergent property intimately linked to the purity of the compartments.
evidence: This is a key conclusion from the model.

claim: Systems showing a well defined polarity with well sorted cisternae exhibit anterograde vesicular fluxes, whereas systems with mixed compartments exhibit retrograde fluxes.
source: Regardless of the details of the model, we find that systems showing a well defined polarity with well sorted cisternae exhibit anterograde vesicular fluxes, whereas systems with mixed compartments exhibit retrograde fluxes.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the model.

claim: Anterograde flux is expected when biochemical conversion is the slowest kinetic process and compartments are long-lived.
source: The former dynamics is expected when biochemical conversion is the slowest kinetic process and compartments are long-lived
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model results.

claim: Retrograde flux is expected when vesicular exchange is slow and the system is composed of transient compartments undergoing individual maturation.
source: while the latter is expected when vesicular exchange is slow and the system is composed of transient compartments undergoing individual maturation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model results.

claim: Maturation of Golgi cisternae has been directly observed in S. cerevisiae, with colocalization of different identity markers within single cisternae (low purity) during maturation.
source: Maturation of Golgi cisternae has been directly observed in S. cerevisiae (Losev et al., 2006), with colocalization of different identity markers within single cisternae (low purity) during maturation
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: Vesicular transport phenotypes have been indirectly observed or inferred through modeling in mammalian cells.
source: whereas vesicular transport phenotypes have been indirectly observed (Dunlop et al., 2017) or inferred through modeling (Dmitrieff et al., 2013) in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature.

claim: A well sorted and polarized Golgi is presumably required to accurately process complex cargo.
source: A well sorted and polarized Golgi is presumably required to accurately process complex cargo.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of Golgi organization.

claim: The glycosylation of secreted cargo is key to the interaction of a vertebrate cell with the immune system of the organism it belongs to.
source: The glycosylation of secreted cargo is key to the interaction of a vertebrate cell with the immune system of the organism it belongs to Ryan and Cobb, 2012
evidence: This is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: Glycans appear to be more diverse in higher eukaryotes - which also possess a highly organized Golgi - than in unicellular eukaryotes like yeast.
source: and glycans appear to be more diverse in higher eukaryotes - which also possess a highly organized Golgi - than in unicellular eukaryotes like yeast (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to literature.

claim: The Golgi organisation in S. cerevisiae could be the result of an adaptation that has favored fast transport over robustness of processing, leading to a less organized Golgi characterized by cisternal maturation and retrograde vesicular transport.
source: The Golgi organisation in S. cerevisiae could thus be the result of an adaptation that has favored fast transport over robustness of processing, leading to a less organized Golgi characterized by cisternal maturation and retrograde vesicular transport.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary adaptation.

claim: The slowing down of Golgi transport when S. cerevisiae is starved in a glucose-free environment coincides with the Golgi becoming more polarized.
source: Remarkably, the slowing down of Golgi transport when S. cerevisiae is starved in a glucose-free environment coincides with the Golgi becoming more polarized (Levi et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental observations.

claim: The model is designed to account for crucial dynamical processes at play in the Golgi with a limited number of parameters.
source: The present model is designed to account for crucial dynamical processes at play in the Golgi with a limited number of parameters.
evidence: This describes the design philosophy of the model.

claim: The model is sufficient to yield robust self-organised structures which can reproduce a number of experimental observations, but cannot be expected to account for the full richness of Golgi dynamics, especially under severe perturbation.
source: It is sufficient to yield robust self-organised structures which can reproduce a number of experimental observations, but cannot be expected to account for the full richness of Golgi dynamics, especially under severe perturbation.
evidence: This acknowledges the limitations of the model.

claim: The model includes a single kind of exchange mechanism based on vesicles.
source: The model includes a single kind of exchange mechanism based on vesicles.
evidence: This describes a feature of the model.

claim: Exchange could also proceed via the pinching and fusion of larger cisterna fragments or via tubular connection between compartments.
source: Exchange could also proceed via the pinching and fusion of larger cisterna fragments (Pfeffer, 2010; Dmitrieff et al., 2013), or via tubular connection between compartments (Trucco et al., 2004)
evidence: This discusses alternative mechanisms with citation support.

claim: The relevance of tubular connections to Golgi transport is still debated.
source: although the relevance of the latter to Golgi transport is still debated (Glick and Luini, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: Stable Golgi tubulation without tubule detachment is observed under brefeldin A treatment, which prevent the membrane association of COPI coat.
source: Stable Golgi tubulation without tubule detachment is observed under brefeldin A treatment, which prevent the membrane association of COPI coat.
evidence: This describes an experimental observation.

claim: Brefeldin A treatment leads to the disappearance of the Golgi by quick resorption into the ER whenever a tubular connection is established between them, in a way suggesting a purely physical (tension-driven) mechanism.
source: This eventually leads to the disappearance of the Golgi by quick resorption into the ER whenever a tubular connection is established between them, in a way suggesting a purely physical (tension-driven) mechanism (Sciaky et al., 1997).
